Spur

SPUR — rhymes with 'blur'; a good word can spur you into motion in a blur of energy. · verb

Hear It

No recording available for this word.

What It Means

To spur to urge, encourage, or stimulate someone into action.

The looming deadline was enough to spur the whole team into working through the weekend.

Worked Example

A runner is exhausted and ready to quit halfway through a marathon. Then she hears the crowd cheering her name from the sidelines, and suddenly she finds the energy to pick up her pace again.

Hearing something that pushes you into renewed action is exactly what it means to be spurred on. Unlike 'force,' which implies no choice at all, to spur means to encourage or motivate someone toward action.

How Spur Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

prompt

prompt: to cause someone to do something

motivate

motivate: to give someone a reason to act

incite

incite: to stir someone into action, often strong action

Antonyms

discourage

discourage: to make someone less willing to do something

deter

deter: to prevent or discourage someone from acting

How Strong Is It? — encourage → incite → spur

encourage vs. spur

encourage vs. spur: Encourage is a plainer, weaker word than spur — encouraging just offers support, while to spur someone means actively pushing them into immediate action.

incite vs. spur

incite vs. spur: Incite is stronger than spur: spurring someone motivates them toward positive action, but inciting often pushes people toward more intense or even reckless action.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — spur-

root — spur-: to kick, to drive on (Old English/Germanic)

Put it together

Put it together: Spur comes from Old English spura, related to spurnan (to kick, to spurn), and originally named the pointed metal device riders use to kick a horse into motion — the verb kept that same sense of driving something into action.

Use the root in a new word: spurn

Use the root in a new word: spurn: She decided to spurn the unfair offer and walk away from the negotiation table.
